canonical_statement: For each Euclidean dimension n >= 1 and exponent 1 < p < infinity, there is a constant C(n,p) such that every real-valued smooth compactly supported function u on R^n satisfies the L^p norm estimate for its Hessian by C(n,p) times the L^p norm of its Laplacian.
domain_and_universes: Provisional: n : Nat with 1 <= n; p : Real with 1 < p; u : R^n -> R smooth with compact support; all analytic encodings require statement-phase selection
quantifiers: for every real exponent p with 1 < p < infinity
there exists C depending only on n and p
for every real-valued compactly supported smooth u on R^n
conclusion: The L^p norm of the Hessian of u is at most C(n,p) times the L^p norm of the Laplacian of u.
boundary_and_exclusions: No strong-type endpoint claim at p = 1 or p = infinity
No bounded-domain estimate or boundary condition
No weighted, parabolic, vector-valued, or variable-coefficient generalization
No lower-order norm term is included in the whole-space compact-support formulation

alternate_encodings.target: componentwise estimates for each second partial derivative
W^{2,p} estimate for a completed Sobolev-space domain
singular-integral boundedness of second derivatives of the Newtonian potential
